newsitem.title: USA: Hicks, Muse company to buy Bumble Bee.
newsitem.headline: Hicks, Muse company to buy Bumble Bee.

text.p: Canned tuna producer Bumble Bee Seafoods Inc. said Friday it filed for bankruptcy protection and agreed to be acquired by a company owned by Dallas investment firm Hicks, Muse, Tate & Furst Inc. for about $163 million.

Under the deal, International Home Foods Inc., which is owned by Hicks, Muse, will acquire substantially all of the assets of Bumble Bee and its subsidiaries for $163 million in cash and the assumption of certain liabilities.
Bumble Bee, the No. 2 U.S. producer of canned tuna and a subsidiary of Thailand's Unicord Public Co. Ltd., filed for bankruptcy protection in order to facilitate its sale.

"It is expected that the Chapter 11 proceedings will have virtually no impact on the operations of the company and the sale hopefully will close within 45 to 60 days," said Bumble Bee President John Batt.
"The Bumble Bee brand has been the mark of premium-quality seafood products in the U.S. for 100 years, and we intend for it to continue to be so for many years to come," he said.
The company said it expected the sale to close within 45 to 60 days.
Bumble Bee filed its bankruptcy petition in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of California in San Diego. Not included in the filing was Bumble Bee's Ecuador affiliate, SEAFMAN.
